limitations: No proof of concrete wire decoder/encoder injectivity or that exact bytes determine structured request; adapter is trusted and must be tested.
No proof of Alloy parser/printer, source-span correspondence, Java or TypeScript refinement, SQL atomicity or browser behavior.
State transitions are serialized abstract steps, not database linearizability; concurrency implementation is a trust/test boundary.
No executable decision procedure completeness theorem, complete full-palette acceptance/denial witness matrix or finite adapter oracle differential exists yet.
Occurrence paths are checked for existence and exact source binding, not proven to denote the parser-reported source construct.
Admission caps revisions and receipts; transition closure never deletes and has no time model.
Request digest consistency and canonical bytes are adapter obligations; byte equality controls replay and collisions.
Wire node-ID uniqueness, exact printer alpha-equivalence and complete command options require explicit adapter correspondence.
